dimensions.rationale: Covers required metrics, trend, segments, anomalies, events, and all required states, with complete rendered evidence; meaningful deduction because no comparison-period control is implemented.
Status, anomaly cause, supporting context, and segment inspection are quickly scannable, but the missing period-change flow blocks one required evaluator task.
Clear hierarchy and restrained operational styling, but still leans on dashboard panels/cards and leaves some desktop space underused.
Cause-first language is brief-specific, but the overall information architecture remains conventional SaaS dashboard grammar.
Native controls, visible focus styles, textual chart meaning, and reduced-motion CSS are present; uncertainty remains because no real automated axe output is recorded.
Objective gate was 28/28 and screenshots exist for all required viewports/states; mobile layouts are usable though vertically long and somewhat cramped.
Loading, populated, empty, partial, and error render deliberately, with missing comparison/no anomaly/zero revenue/large value stress cases handled.
Consistent tokens, focus treatment, panels, and segmented controls are used across states.
Small dependency-free implementation with escaped fixture output and a local check script, but limited tests and no comparison-period logic.
Static dependency-free app with successful rendered evidence and no heavy runtime assets observed.
Handles required content stress cases, but fidelity is reduced by the absent period mutation/control.
Uses deterministic local fixture data with no live commercial data dependency observed.
Frozen evidence shows the app is inspectable across the full objective matrix, with Candidate A recorded at 28/28 objective gates.

uncertainty: Automated accessibility scan output is missing, so accessibility success is not inferred beyond observable source and screenshots.
conclusion: Candidate A is the stronger frozen submission overall: it misses the comparison-period flow but has complete objective render evidence and no recorded serious axe failures.
